hypothesis: The kernel-sync cost class (the compact-refine decompose's reported-only 8.0ms compact-tail) is the daemon<->kernel state-sync machinery: S1 the 1500ms-debounced full-namespace dill snapshot armed after every settled cell (repl.py _snapshot_state: single-pass per-variable dill.dump into a staged temp + manifest + two renames, NO fsync), S2 the compact-time sync_after_compaction (prune+list+durable notice row), S3 the dispose flush at kernel teardown, S4 the boot restore. All four are TS-parity port-faithful (agent-session.ts:8604 _syncKernelStateAfterCompaction, repl-manager.ts:964 execute->scheduleSnapshot, :1713 the 1500ms debounce, shared.ts:8-9) and serialize on the kernel's SINGLE request queue (requests.rs enqueue_request), so a dump can delay the next cell and rides the compact/teardown walls. The uncharacterized dimensions: the dump cost's size/shape scaling, the recurrence count per session activity, the queue-block interference, and which syncs are load-bearing vs cuttable. Honest negatives (structural/TS-parity-locked) are valid outcomes; candidates are reported with measured bounds.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY, no product change (decompose lane; the record is the deliverable). Pinned tip e2ee82f2d (origin/rust). VM h7nun5ywykfjsx5edgg4scrv (hillclimb-perf-kernel-sync, ubuntu:22.04 16c/32GB/100GB, rustup 1.98.1), cargo build --release --locked --workspace rc=0, binary sha ae1b2a1b... Bench harness deployed + settled (kernel-venv warm at /root/bench/global/rust). Fixtures: the fleet-known 256KiB session bd18b080... (the compact's other phases already decomposed; the kernel-sync spans are the target) + the 10MiB stock dadaecfc... for the big-file compact boundary. REAL assembly, offline mock (prime-inference/mock-1; queues: turn/summarizer/refiner, live script rewrites per turn) - the cells run through the REAL agent path (prompt -> model toolCall -> ipython tool -> kernel). NAMESPACE SIZE CLASSES built in-kernel per trial: E (boot ns only), B64k/B1m/B8m/B32m (8 strings x 8KiB/128KiB/1MiB/4MiB), O8m (8 nested dict/list trees, CPU-heavy pickle), OCAP (one 20MiB var over the 16MiB per-variable cap + 8x1MiB). INSTRUMENT: the in-tree PA_COMPACTION_TRACE seam (the S2 spans), an artifact-dir commit watcher (payload/manifest mtime+size at 25ms polls - every S1/S2a/S3 commit), a /proc CPU sampler (kernel+daemon utime+stime at 10ms), arrival-accurate frame pump (the cell windows from tool_execution frames), the raw-kernel substrate legs (the product venv's python -m rlm.repl driven over its JSONL protocol: the dump/prune/list/restore/EOF-flush walls per class, n=18 dumps/class/pass), and census legs under strace (fd-map v2.1, structure-only). LEGS (same-VM sequential, per-block probe_v09 preflights + pre/mid/post, binary sha assert per block, quiet gate, product-only zombie sweep, per-trial fixture prehash): raw1/raw2 (ascending/descending class order), prod1/prod2 (the product legs: build turn -> S1 watch -> trivial control turn -> rebuild turn -> interference turn submitted INTO the fire window -> compact (S2) -> get_state -> stdin close (S3 wall)), bigcompact (E/B8m on the 10MiB fixture), restore (a second spawn resuming the mutated session with the first spawn's agent dir - the S4 boot+restore), census (1/class). The interference ABBA is inside each trial: the tD cell (submitted at the estimated fire+~40ms) vs the tB control cell, same trial, same namespace; the artifact events classify in-window vs missed post-hoc.
parity_notes: No product source changed in any phase; frozen parity untouched (the RPC surface exercised as a black box over stdio; PA_COMPACTION_TRACE is the product's own off-by-default debug env). Driver-side findings, all mine, all disclosed: (1) the mock's prompt-response is the ADMISSION, not the turn end - the per-turn walls/cell windows are derived from the frame stream (agent/turn/tool_execution frames), not the response receipt. (2) the interference submit lands at the estimated fire (the tC cell's tool_execution_end + 1500ms) + ~40ms (the prompt->cell model roundtrip), so only dump walls >~40ms are hitable from the prompt path (B32m's 29ms window is missed by design - its bound is the raw dump wall; O8m's 530ms window is hit solidly). (3) the artifact watcher's poll resolution is 25ms; commit INSTANTS come from the payload mtime_ns; the watcher's tmp sightings bound the dump windows conservatively. (4) the probe-frame pump's idle drain had the ctxrebuild-lane select-park shape (an idle channel blocked the full max_s): fixed to bound the select wait by the idle deadline BEFORE the legs (the pilot trials' 8s-per-block artifacts disclosed; no leg ran with it). (5) A discovery-lag caveat: the watcher finds the artifact dir only after the first payload exists, so a trial's FIRST commit may be recorded at discovery rather than at its poll - the mtime_ns is always the true commit. (6) the census legs run under strace: structure-only, INVALID for timing. (7) the raw legs' CPU deltas are 100Hz-tick coarse (<10ms unresolvable); the O8m-class CPU (530ms) is resolvable and equals the wall (CPU-bound). (8) one B64k trial's ready_ms=1107 (a cold-boot outlier, disclosed in validity).

validity.notes: All legs ran in the D-regime at every boundary (CLASS=D), with the depth DEEPENING monotonically through the campaign (A_P50 33 -> 110 -> 145ms): the durable-row spans (S2c, the compaction row, the exit floor's regime component) are regime-contaminated and depth-varying across blocks - the S2c numbers are reported as the bimodal fast-path/wall distribution they are, and the CPU-phase spans (the dumps, the O8m interference, the raw walls) are regime-independent (pass-to-pass raw p50s agree within ~2-5%). The interference instrument resolves only dump walls >~40ms (the prompt->cell model roundtrip lands the cell ~40ms after the submit; B32m's 29ms window is missed by design - its bound is the raw dump wall; O8m's 530ms window is hit 8/8). The product-side dump windows are poll-bounded (25ms); the O8m windows (p50 527ms) corroborate the raw walls. The raw legs' CPU deltas are 100Hz-tick coarse (<10ms unresolvable; the O8m CPU 525-530ms equals its wall - the dump is CPU-bound there). One B64k trial's ready_ms=1107 (a cold-boot outlier, kept, disclosed). The census trials under strace: structure-only, INVALID for timing; the B8m census trial shows 12 dumps (the strace overhead shifted the debounce/queue interleavings - disclosed). 5 of the 11 skill modules are unpicklable (_PrimeAgentCallableSkillModule instances: dill skips them every dump - the manifest savedNames carries only 6 skills + user names; the notice's list_names reports all 20) - a per-dump skip overhead, structural, ~free. The snapshot payload writes carry NO fsync (staged temp + two renames only - the crash-freshness window is the rename), so the D-regime's fresh-write wall applies to the session-jsonl fdatasyncs (S2c), not the payload writes. The EOF-flush legs (raw) measure the CRASH path (stdin close without a shutdown request); the product's graceful teardown sends the shutdown request first, so the runtime's EOF flush never runs there (verified in teardown.rs + the exit walls carry only the dispose flush). The restore legs prove the S4 revive through the shared agent dir (manifest savedN=15 at B8m) but the restore wall itself is a PREWARM-path (background) cost - the raw legs carry its wall per class.

candidates_reported_only: C1 THE RECURRING RE-DUMP (the biggest): S1 re-serializes the ENTIRE namespace after every cell burst even when nothing changed - the tB trivial cell (xt=1) re-dumped the full 8.4MiB at B8m and the 2MB tree at ~530ms CPU at O8m; every settled cell pays a full dump of everything. A per-variable freshness memo (re-dump only changed names; the payload is per-variable records) would cut the recurring fire to the changed-vars cost: O8m 530ms -> ~ms when unchanged; B32m 29ms -> ~ms. BOUND: the recurring cost is the full dump wall per burst, measured per class. PARITY SURFACE: the payload format is internal BUT cross-product (the same session resumed by the TS product must restore a rust-written payload and vice versa; the shared runtime's version marker governs) - an incremental format needs a version bump + both-side readers; a substantial lane, not a clean single-side cut.

C2 THE COMPACT-TIME PRUNE REDUNDANCY: at compact, S2a re-dumps the namespace that the last S1 fire committed when no cell ran between (every trial: the prune's commit is byte-identical in size to the last fire's commit, zero settled executions between). A skip-if-fresh (the committed manifest stat + the no-settled-execution-since counter, both already tracked in snapshot.rs's skip machinery) would save the prune span on the compact wall: O8m 509ms -> ~0 (the compact 730 -> ~220ms); B32m 33 -> ~0; at the stock-fixture classes only ~3-8ms (vs the 88-135ms regime walls on the same command - immaterial there). PARITY: TS prunes UNCONDITIONALLY (agent-session.ts:8606) - an internal-behavior divergence needing a TS-parity case + a served-path assertion oracle (the notice bytes identical when fresh; the stale path still dumps AND prunes - the live-ns cap enforcement must not be skipped when anything settled).

C3 THE QUEUE-BLOCK INTERFERENCE: the dump shares the kernel's single request queue with cells; a cell landing mid-dump waits the full wall (O8m p50 325ms, in-window 8/8 vs the 1ms control). The C1 memo shrinks the dump below notice; alternatively a chunked dump (yield the queue between per-variable records) bounds the block to one record's cost - a runtime change, TS-divergent (the TS kernel blocks identically), and it stretches the dump wall. BOUND: the block = the in-flight dump wall.
C4 THE DISPOSE FLUSH: the same dump-wall bound inside the exit wall (B32m exit 63.5 vs the 31.4 floor; O8m 614). The C1 memo bounds it identically; no standalone cut.

decision: The kernel-sync class is decomposed end-to-end across the size/shape classes. ANSWER: the reported-only 8.0ms compact-tail from the compact-refine record is the SMALL end of a four-sync class whose cost is OBJECT-SHAPE-bound, not size-bound: the strings scale at ~0.9ms/MiB (page-cache memcpy, regime-light) while a nested-object namespace scales at ~260ms per MiB-PICKLED (100% CPU dill.dump - the O8m class: a 530ms dump for a 2MB-pickled tree). The four syncs: S1 arms after EVERY settled cell (one full-namespace dump per burst; the boot fire is skipped by the rust-only restore_boot_hold arm), S2's prune span is the dump wall + ~2.8ms on the compact's critical path (3.1ms at the boot ns -> 509.5ms at the object class = 70% of that compact's 730ms wall), S3's dispose flush rides the exit wall (31.4ms floor; +32ms at 32MiB; 614ms at the object class), S4's restore is the unpickle wall on the prewarm path (4.2ms -> 158ms). THE MECHANISM FINDING: the kernel's SINGLE request queue serializes every dump with cells - a cell landing mid-dump waits the full wall (O8m: 325ms p50 vs the 1ms control, in-window 8/8) - and the debounced dump fires after every cell burst, so an object-heavy session pays the full dump repeatedly (6-7 dumps per measured trial) AND blocks the next cell behind it. The S2c notice row and the compaction row are regime-bound (the D-class fdatasync walls, 0.7-9ms fast path vs 88-135ms deep-D, plus the fresh payload's writeback interplay); S2b is 0.1-0.5ms; the whole S2 spans are session-size-INDEPENDENT (the 10MiB-fixture legs match the 256KiB ones). HONEST NEGATIVE ON THE CUT QUESTION: the four-sync structure is TS-parity port-faithful and load-bearing (crash-resume freshness, the 16MiB per-variable cap policy verified end-to-end on OCAP, the #227 notice semantics, the resume contract); at the stock-fixture classes the kernel-sync spans (3-8ms) are immaterial next to the regime walls (88-135ms) on the same command, so NO cut is warranted there; at object-heavy namespaces the signal is real and large, and the two candidate cuts (C1 the per-variable freshness memo - the recurring re-dump; C2 the compact-time skip-if-fresh - the redundant prune) have measured bounds but each carries a parity surface (C1 the cross-product payload format; C2 the TS-unconditional-prune divergence) that needs its own implementation lane with the full oracle discipline. One parity-ledger finding shipped with the record: the rust-only restore_boot_hold boot-fire skip (TS fires the tiny boot dump at every boot; rust never does).
